audit_findings.title: Acquisition-created intangible assets may be treated as costless renewable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $984m of 2025 identifiable-intangible amortization, equal to 56.3% of the $1,748.4m OE anchor; $1,714m of 2025 acquisition spending
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization without deducting the recurring economic cost of replacing customer relationships, backlog, software and databases inflates anchor OE and may also make acquisition-supported growth appear organic.
audit_findings.evidence: The $30 million increase in depreciation and amortization in 2025 as compared to 2024 was primarily the result of an increase in amortization of capitalized software and of intangible assets from acquisitions occurring in 2024 and 2025, offset by less amortization of certain intangible assets from the merger between Quintiles and IMS Health.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions and acquired intangibles are economically significant, but it does not establish what portion of amortization represents maintenance reinvestment. Even a minority of the $984m amortization would be large relative to anchor OE, so the unresolved treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every component of the $984m amortization to the OE calculation, estimate maintenance replacement spending by intangible category, and rerun all scenarios using acquisition-neutral OE and organic growth.

audit_findings.title: Customer advances may be capitalized in OE and added again as cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $339m 2025 increase in unearned income, equal to 19.4% of anchor OE; $242m reported 2025 operating-cash-flow contribution; $2,080m cash/STI bridge addition, equal to $12.19 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A contract-liability increase can temporarily raise cash-flow-derived OE, while treating customer-funded operating liquidity as surplus cash can add the same financing benefit again through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Unearned income consists of advance payments and billings in excess of revenues recognized.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability increase and cash-flow benefit are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether OE normalized them or how much of bridge cash is excess. The amounts are large relative to both anchor OE and per-share value, making the possible double count material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 and first-half 2026 unearned-income movements through OE, normalize the anchor for nonrecurring customer advances, determine required operating liquidity and restricted/customer-funded cash, and rerun the valuation and bridge.

audit_findings.title: The consolidated cash numerator may include value belonging to noncontrolling interests
audit_findings.magnitude: $130m NCI at June 30, 2026, equal to 0.48% of $27,170m base equity value and $0.76 per diluted share; $3m of first-half 2026 net income attributed to NCI
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated operating cash flow and reinvestment can include subsidiary economics not attributable to parent shareholders, requiring either parent-attributable OE or an NCI bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the NCI as of the acquisition date was based on fair value assessments, primarily using an income approach and applying the NCI’s ownership percentage.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership mismatch remains possible, but the filed NCI carrying amount provides a concrete scale: a full $130m deduction would reduce base value by only about $0.76 per share and would not materially alter the valuation conclusion. Current attributed earnings are also small.
audit_findings.action: Confirm parent-attributable treatment in the OE workbook and add a documented NCI deduction if needed; no full scenario redesign is required unless later filings show a substantially larger NCI claim.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded investment commitments may not be netted against added stakes
audit_findings.magnitude: $413m unfunded commitments, equal to 78.7% of the $525m stakes bridge and $2.42 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Future capital calls consume cash before common-holder distributions, but they may also purchase additional fund interests whose value is absent from the current stakes balance.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have funded approximately $339 million of these commitments and we have approximately $413 million remaining to be funded which has not been included in the above table as we are unable to predict when these commitments will be paid.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is demonstrated and is large relative to the stakes addition, but deducting all $413m without valuing the interests acquired would also be incomplete. The record does not establish whether stakes_net already reflects the commitments or whether future acquired interests offset the calls, so materiality cannot be resolved from the supplied bridge.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the stakes_net schedule by fund, reconcile carrying or fair values and remaining commitments, estimate the value received for future calls, and rerun the bridge using net economic exposure.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration appears outside both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $104m contingent-consideration liability at June 30, 2026, equal to 0.38% of $27,170m base equity value and $0.61 per diluted share; $15m of first-half 2026 contingent/deferred purchase-price payments
audit_findings.mechanism: Financing-classified acquisition payments can bypass cash-flow-derived OE and therefore require recognition as an acquisition cost or an equity-bridge liability.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 the Company has accrued approximately 67 % of the maximum contingent consideration payments that could potentially become payable.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed liability is a demonstrated acquisition claim, and no corresponding bridge deduction is shown. Nevertheless, deducting the entire $104m would change base value by only about $0.61 per share, which is not material relative to $159.20 base value or the gap to the $267.77 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $104m liability and all deferred purchase-price balances to OE and bridge items, then deduct any unrecognized amount in the next valuation update.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease replacement cost can escape a cash-flow-based OE calculation
audit_findings.magnitude: $218m finance-lease liability and $326m undiscounted payments at December 31, 2025; $5m of 2025 principal payments, equal to 0.29% of anchor OE; liability equals $1.28 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease depreciation is added back through operating cash flow while principal repayment is classified as financing, potentially omitting the cash cost of maintaining leased operating assets.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance lease expense is recognized as a combination of depreciation expense for the leased asset and interest expense for the outstanding lease liabilities using the discount rate discussed above.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification risk is real, but the filed current cash-cost proxy is only $5m versus $1,748.4m of anchor OE. Even treating the entire $218m liability as an omitted bridge claim would reduce value by about $1.28 per share, so the demonstrated scale is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether OE deducts finance-lease principal or an equivalent maintenance charge and retain a separate finance-lease reconciliation for future periods; revisit if noncash leased-asset additions become materially larger.
